text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; how long do these episodes typically last, and do you ever lose consciousness or fall down?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Focal Impaired Awareness Seizure (likely temporal lobe or frontal lobe etiology).

The patient's description of a "muddy taste" (gustatory aura), followed by staring, automatisms (hand gestures), unresponsiveness, and post-ictal confusion is highly characteristic of a focal seizure. Given the recurrent nature over the past month, I would suspect epilepsy.

I have already received the clinical history from the script. To confirm the diagnosis and localize the focus, do you have any prior EEG results, or should I recommend a routine EEG and an MRI of the brain?
